description: A materials-and-compatibility guide to MyMuse: water-based versus silicone lubricants, condom safety, the 21+ gate and which older shipping claims we could not verify.

Buyers who want to understand discreet delivery and returns from the official store before ordering.

Shoppers relying on the old BUNDLE20, MUSE10 or seven-day-returns statements — we could not verify those terms.

content_blocks.heading: What should a first-time buyer check on MyMuse, and is delivery actually discreet?
content_blocks.body: Start with the material, not the discount. MyMuse's own guide says its water-based Glide is paraben-free, glycerin-free, pH-balanced and safe with silicone massagers and condoms; silicone-based lubricants should not be used with silicone devices. The store states free, discreet and express delivery with COD, and applies a 21+ age gate. We could not verify the old BUNDLE20 or MUSE10 codes, the exact unmarked-box description or the seven-day returns claim, so they are not presented as facts.

items.title: The material-and-compatibility matrix
items.body: Water-based lubricant: compatible with silicone massagers, latex, polyurethane and polyisoprene condoms; washes off with water; may need reapplication. Silicone-based lubricant: condom-compatible and longer-lasting, but the brand warns it can degrade silicone devices. Oil-based products: CDC says petroleum jelly, body lotion and cooking oils can weaken latex condoms and cause breakage. For a first purchase with silicone toys, water-based is the least complicated choice.

items.title: Glide — what the official guide actually states
items.body: MyMuse's guide lists Glide water-based lubricant at ₹699, described as paraben-free, glycerin-free, fragrance-free, pH-balanced and made with organic aloe vera extract. It says the formula is compatible with all MyMuse massagers and condoms. The guide also recommends a pH between 3.8 and 4.5 for vaginal use. These are brand statements; we did not see a full INCI or an independent pH measurement.

items.title: Cost and what we cannot calculate
items.body: The guide gives ₹699 for Glide but we could not verify a stated bottle volume on the official page we read, so a cost per use would be guesswork. Marketplace listings show different pack sizes and prices, but they are not the official store. We also saw a Link+ C-shaped massager at ₹4999 against ₹6999 on the storefront, and a free travel pouch on orders above ₹3,499 — both are snapshots, not promises.

items.title: Discretion and the age gate
items.body: The storefront displays 'FREE, DISCREET & EXPRESS DELIVERY' and 'COD AVAILABLE', and opens with a 'Are you over 21?' gate. Brand claims also mention discreet packaging and billing, body-safe materials, a 100-day warranty and 3.75 lakh plus customers. Older Durza copy described unmarked kraft boxes, a generic 'personal care' courier sticker, a two-to-three-day shipping window and a seven-day returns rule; we could not verify those specifics and have removed them.

items.title: Comfort product, not treatment
items.body: Using a lubricant is normal and does not signal a problem. MyMuse's own guide says so and advises consulting a healthcare professional if dryness is persistent. Nothing on this page is a treatment for infection, hormonal symptoms or pain. If something hurts, stop and get clinical advice rather than trying another product.

content_blocks.text: We checked the official MyMuse storefront and lubricant guide, and CDC condom-use guidance, on 26 Nov 2026. We did not buy, use or test any product. Older Durza claims about specific coupon codes, packaging text, delivery times and a seven-day returns window could not be verified and are not repeated as facts. Lubricants and massagers are comfort products, not medical treatments. Durza earns a commission on qualifying purchases through tracked links at no extra cost to you.

items.q: Which lubricant should I buy first?
items.a: If you have silicone massagers or use condoms, a water-based lubricant is the simplest choice. MyMuse's guide says its Glide formula is compatible with both, and CDC recommends water-based or silicone-based lubricants with condoms. Avoid oil-based products with latex condoms.

The storefront states 'FREE, DISCREET & EXPRESS DELIVERY' and mentions discreet packaging and billing. We could not verify the older description of unmarked kraft boxes and a generic courier sticker, so we do not promise that exact format.

items.q: Can I use silicone lubricant with my silicone massager?
items.a: No. MyMuse's own guide warns that silicone-based lubricant can degrade silicone devices over time. Use water-based with silicone toys; silicone lubricant is fine with condoms but needs soap to wash off.
It can improve comfort and reduce friction, but it is not a treatment for an underlying cause. The brand's guide itself advises consulting a healthcare professional if dryness is persistent.
No. We read official and CDC guidance on 26 Nov 2026, purchased nothing and make no medical claims.
